newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Sweden's Riksbank seen cutting rates more.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sweden's Riksbank seen cutting rates more.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday surprised the market with a larger-than-expected 25 basis point cut in a key interest rate and analysts forecast more cuts before the year's end.
The Riksbank trimmed its repo rate to 4.35 percent, exceeding most analysts' expectations which ranged between five and 25 basis points, saying inflation remained on target.

Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom on Monday said he was satisfied with inflationary data over the past month, with Swedish consumer prices unchanged in October and producing a year-on-year rate of minus 0.1 percent. It was the first time since 1959 that Sweden has seen prices fall.
With all signs pointing to inflation staying under control in the near future, analysts said the Riksbank could cut its repo rate at least one more time in 1996.
"There will be new speculation about further repo rate cuts because fundamentals show there's still potential for further monetary easing," Unibank Markets analyst Bjorn Englund said.
"We should perhaps also see one to two more rate cuts in 1997 although it will depend on the crown and wages," Den Danske Bank economist Anders Borschsenius said.

The Riksbank said the cut to the repo rate, the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity, was permissible because inflation was in line with its target of two percent with a one percentage point variance in either direction.
"The Riksbank judges that the outlook for inflation continues to be in line with the inflation target," the bank said in a statement.

Ahead of the repo announcement, analysts were mixed on whether the Riksbank would again lower the repo rate, which began the year at 8.91 percent, or wait until after its next inflation report is released on December 17.

The move prompted Swedish debt markets to firm slightly, with six-month Treasury bill rates tumbling nine basis points to 4.31 percent and the 10-year bond yield falling seven basis points to 7.12 percent.
"Rate cuts can be expected to continue, with the repo rate falling to 4.0 percent in the first quarter of next year," James McKay, analyst at PaineWebber International, said in a statement.
"The next focus will be the Riksbank's inflation report on due December 17."
The bank said that for administrative reasons as well as because of the Christmas and New Year holidays, the repo operation to be announced on December 17 will run for three weeks.

"There will be speculation at least on December 17, the same day that the inflation report will be released, that there will be futher repo rate cuts -- as that one will keep steady for three weeks' time," Englund said.
Markets will also be looking for a cut to the interest rate corridor, marked out by the deposit and lending rates, at the Riksbank's next board meeting on December 5, analysts said.
The deposit and lending rates currently stand at 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent. They were last lowered by 50 basis points on October 24.
